sources.note: Beat S05-B02: 'Take a standard 52-card deck and shuffle it. Deal it evenly.' The motion answers the word 'shuffle'; no narration is quoted on screen.
The stock clip at about 9:30 was a deck cut that froze; Devin asked for an actual shuffle, animated is fine. This asset replaces BROLL-01 at the shuffle cues.

shared_dependencies.what: card() primitive (win95-workbench-1.1.0): the blue diamond-lattice back and the regular playing-card faces with corner index, pip layouts and court marks
reference renders of the same primitives; not embedded, the scenes draw the primitives directly at 240 × 336 px

authored_additions: Top-down stylised riffle: the squared deck splits into two tilted halves; each half releases cards from its top into a centre pile in a seeded, mostly alternating order (26 from each side); the ragged pile squares up. A top-down 'lift' arc and a scale bump stand in for the cards springing off the thumbs. Not a physical simulation.

The deck's initial order is a seeded Fisher–Yates permutation of the 52 cards (seed 20260916); it only matters for which faces flash. Main riffle: 8S, 6S, QS, 6H flash. Loop: 8C, 2H, 9C, QS flash. Every card lands face down.
The loop timeline continues from the main timeline's riffled order (apart → riffle → square → split → apart) so its first and last authored frames are identical.
fonts_at_render: Liberation Sans (C:/WINDOWS/fonts/LiberationSans-Regular.ttf and -Bold.ttf via fc-match) for the flashed faces' index and pips; rendered media does not depend on the viewer's fonts.
